## 1. Continuous Batching & Inference Server Mechanics

### 1.1 Traditional vs. Continuous Batching
In naive static batching, an inference server processes requests in fixed batches (e.g., batch size 8). If 7 requests arrive at $t=0$ and 1 arrives at $t=50$, the server either idles compute resources waiting for the 8th, or incurs massive queueing delays.

**Continuous Batching (Dynamic Batching)** dynamically groups active requests into batches at every decoding step based on instantaneous available slots and memory capacity. The scheduler evaluates the queue at each token generation interval and packs as many waiting/active sequences as hardware constraints permit.
